items.summary: Carolyn Marvin, a semi-retired University of Pennsylvania communications professor and former author of When Old Technologies Were New, blocks UberEats food delivery robots on busy sidewalks as protest against their presence in public space. After being handcuffed for blocking a robot she was holding out food to, Marvin intends to contest her disorderly conduct ticket. She argues the robots threaten jobs and pose hazards to people with mobility issues, while others worry about denying paid orders. Onlookers react mixed—some cheer her as 'the queen,' citing distrust of AI; passing children are drawn by the robots' humanizing Halloween graphics added by Avride, which operates nearly 1,000 machines across campuses and cities like Jersey City and Austin. Marvin says she wants people to know they have a say in whether private robots belong on public streets.
items.title: Professor Blocks Food Delivery Robots in Philadelphia Protest

items.summary: Thailand paused construction on 49 datacentre projects and approval decisions on 117 more in September 2026, amid concerns about insufficient regulatory detail. The shift follows a broader regional reassessment: Indonesia halted one project over missing permits, while Singapore had earlier imposed a moratorium from 2019 to 2022 for water and electricity use. Wood Mackenzie estimates Johor’s datacentres already consume 24% of the state’s power, potentially rising to 40% by 2035, and that operational sites need about 675m cubic meters of water per day. Analysts warn of grid bottlenecks and uneven benefit-sharing as investment accelerates amid AI-driven demand.
items.title: Southeast Asia Pauses Datacentre Expansion Over Resource Strain

items.summary: Cooperative bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa was targeted in a cyberattack that enabled fraudulent transactions of up to $133 million. The attacker used the bank's own account rather than customers' accounts and converted funds into USDC and USDT stablecoins, leaving customer assets unaffected. Arkéa suspended certain systems and reassured clients there is no impact on their assets while operations return to normal.
items.title: Hackers pull off $133 million French bank heist via service provider

items.summary: CTM360 reports a surge in fraudulent reward portals and fake gift card giveaways that trap users through deceptive verification loops and paid subscriptions. Based on activity observed by CTM360, analysts identified more than 1,000 incidents linked to this recurring campaign. The campaigns impersonate established brands such as PlayStation, Sephora, SHEIN, Walmart, and Amazon, using cloned logos, fake participant numbers, countdown timers, and fabricated celebrity endorsements like MrBeast or Alix Earle. Victims are lured with a free gift card pitch requiring a 'human verification' step that never delivers the reward; instead they complete surveys, install unwanted applications, or subscribe to paid mobile services via carrier billing.
items.title: CTM360 Exposes Fake Gift Card Scams Exploiting Trusted Brands

items.summary: A California judge has deemed Tesla liable for fraud in a lawsuit brought by homeowner Ambrose Conroy over an unfinished and unpermitted Solar Roof installation. Tesla had already conceded breach of contract, warranty violation, and negligence. The court sanctioned Tesla twice before ruling on September 11 that it acted willfully, restricting the trial to compensatory and punitive damages. Internal emails reportedly described the home as a test of whether Tesla could do “any job,” though Electrek notes the texts themselves have not been seen. Conroy estimates repair costs at well over $2. 5 million after Tesla offered just $5,000. Tesla is now petitioning the California Court of Appeal to freeze the case, arguing the order violates due process and amounts to a directed verdict before trial. A December 4 readiness conference precedes any possible December trial. Electrek has been covering Solar Roof since its 2016 unveiling by Elon Musk.
items.title: California Judge Holds Tesla Liable for Solar Roof Fraud After Evidence Failures

items.summary: CleanTechnica reports that General Motors is celebrating the 30th anniversary of its ill-fated EV1 sedan, positioning it as a pioneering step in vehicle electrification. The article notes GM produced barely more than 1,000 units overall before recalling them in 2003. This celebration coincides with Tesla CEO Elon Musk canceling his Cybertruck, leaving the pickup market open. GM frames its EV1 work as predating Tesla's 2003 launch and highlights firsts like heat pumps and regenerative braking. The piece questions whether EV1 was truly a flop in sales but not technology, while noting broader US EV market shifts after federal tax credit changes.
items.title: GM Revives EV1 Legacy as Cybertruck Ends

items.summary: Researchers at Middle Technical University in Baghdad report a solar-panel cooling system that could boost efficiency in hot climates. Summer heat typically reduces silicon panel efficiency by 0. 5 percent per degree above 25 °C, and panels can reach surfaces near 80 °C where efficiency may drop up to 25 percent. The new design pairs an evaporative cellulose pad on the panel's back with intermittent front-surface water spraying triggered at 42–45 °C. In its best configuration—a 100-millimeter-thick pad—the system dropped panel temperature by 29. 7 °C and improved electrical efficiency by about 20 percent, raising a 150-watt module's output by roughly 16. 7 W during July through September tests. Lead author Deyaa M. N. Mahmood notes the cooled rear air could pre-cool building ventilation.
items.title: Iraqi Researchers Cool Solar Panels With Water Evaporative System

items.summary: Armenian officials have begun design work on the TRIPP trade corridor, even as a US operating agreement stays unfinished. Armenia’s parliament approved forming TRIPP Development in late October; Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said preparatory work would start immediately and could include roads, railways, power lines and pipelines. Iran and Russia oppose the route over fears of disrupted north-south trade and a possible US security presence. At a Brussels forum on November 4, Pashinyan predicted Armenia could apply for EU membership by 2028.
items.title: Armenia Launches Design Work for Trump-Backed TRIPP Trade Corridor Amid Regional Pushback

items.summary: In southeastern Massachusetts, two cranberry bogs in Kingston and Plymouth are the first known sites to grow berries beneath an operating solar installation. Growers harvest ruby-red berries while pickers move around metal poles shaded by panels. The projects, built this fall for a second season under them, were created by clean energy developer Greenbacker Renewables with Distributed Energy Infrastructure managing construction and Iain Ward overseeing the crops. Massachusetts promotes such agrivoltaics to reach net-zero carbon emissions by 2050 while using protected cranberry wetlands that cannot be developed.
items.title: Massachusetts Cranberry Bogs Add Solar Panels Above Harvested Berries

items.summary:
As negotiators gather for the annual UN climate summit, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change faces gridlock. The panel suspended its October meeting without approving next year's budget or a report timetable. More than 100 scientists signed an open letter urging adequate resources and equitable country voices. Next year's funding remains uncertain, though nations may push harder at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey. Governments voluntarily set the annual $9.7 million budget, roughly movie-production cost. Bob Kopp of Rutgers said U.S. federal withdrawal likely stalled progress; Davide Faranda warned climate information could be weaponized if collaboration breaks down; Mike Hulme of Cambridge noted deepening political tensions slow the work.

visual null},
items.title: IPCC Stalls Over Funding and Political Tensions Before COP31

items.summary: The article reports that several U.S. hydrogen development projects have stalled amid funding uncertainty under the Trump administration and weak demand. In November 2024, the Biden administration had announced up to $2.2 billion in award commitments for two Regional Clean Hydrogen Hubs out of a total of $7 billion across seven hubs. The MACH2 hub received a $750 million Department of Energy award, while ARCH2 was expected to receive $925 million. Air Products cancelled its $4.5 billion Louisiana project after reporting approximately $2.9 billion in pretax charges, and Exxon Mobil paused a Baytown facility that could produce up to 1 billion cubic feet of blue hydrogen per day; the firm said it had invested around $500 million and cited weak customer demand. Tom Torres stated he does not think the hubs are happening until evidence suggests otherwise.
items.title: US Hydrogen Hubs Stall on Funding Cuts and Weak Demand

items.summary: Electric truck maker Workhorse is introducing its W56 Class 5 and 6 electric trucks to Canada through a new agreement with Tristan Fleet Management, marking the company's first-ever Canadian dealer partnership. The deal adds sales, parts, repair, and round-the-clock roadside support nationwide. Workhorse highlights years of Canadian deployments since 2021 and cites high fuel costs as boosting demand for electrification.
items.title: Workhorse W56 Electric Trucks Enter Canada via New Dealer Deal

items.summary: Lighthouse, a subsidiary of Difare Group, inaugurated the 82 MW Faro de San Marcos solar plant on Nov. 5 in Ecuador’s Santa Elena province. The developer says it is the country’s largest operational and privately owned solar facility, with more than 105,000 bifacial modules across 49.3 hectares. It began commercial operation ahead of a first-quarter-2027 schedule; company estimates put annual output at about 106 GWh.
items.title: Ecuador’s Largest Private Solar Plant Begins Commercial Operation

items.summary: On Saturday, Tesla CEO Elon Musk said the company would add a production shift to finish outstanding Cybertruck orders before dismantling the line around June/July next year for planned Cybercab expansion. He noted in an X post that the order backlog far exceeds what Tesla can build before closing.
items.title: Tesla Plans Extra Shift to Clear Cybertruck Orders Before Line Closes for Cybercab Expansion

items.summary: Binance said its finance chief Kaiser Ng is leaving after more than five years, with a transition plan over the last half year, per co-CEO Yi He. Justin Yek takes over as CFO. The departure comes days after hackers stole $6.3 billion in a record heist; Binance will reimburse affected customers and blames a North Korean group, which Pyongyang denies.
items.title: Binance Names New CFO After Chief Finance Officer Departs

items.summary: At its annual general meeting on Saturday, National Trust members voted overwhelmingly—53,256 for and 4,094 against—to seek a new bank that prioritises biodiversity protection and climate action. The resolution instructs the charity to launch a competitive tendering process, though insiders suggest it may take at least a year. Sandy Nairne warned the result is not binding on trustees. Proposer Drew James argued Barclays undermines conservation by financing fossil fuels, while Restore Trust’s Cornelia van der Poll called the vote a distraction from maintaining historic buildings and countryside.
items.title: National Trust votes for ethical banking partner

items.summary: A Great Lakes-based non-profit is preparing as reports suggest the Trump administration may plan four sealed-pod underwater datacenters off Maine and Alaska, though no projects are currently proposed in the region. Activists warn of heat-driven algal blooms and thermal shock from even a 2-5F rise, while Microsoft says it has no plans to deploy an underwater unit at this time. New York’s moratorium ends mid-2027; Ohio recently denied wastewater discharge after public outcry.
items.title: Great Lakes non-profit prepares for underwater datacenters

items.summary: Bharat Traders Television (BTTV) is running a special Muhurat Trading program to mark the start of Samvat 2083. The live session, held on November 8 from 2:00 PM to 3:30 PM, brings together market experts and guests who discuss current trends, investment opportunities, and outlook for the coming year.
items.title: BTTV Broadcasts Muhurat Trading Expert Panel for Samvat 2083

items.summary: Jefferies' Christopher Wood warns that a slowdown in US artificial intelligence spending could weaken economic growth and shift expectations toward Federal Reserve rate cuts, potentially supporting gold. With prices consolidating around $3,800–4,000 per ounce, he cautions investors to avoid treating the range as an assured buying opportunity.
items.title: Jefferies Sees AI Spending Slowdown Could Fuel Gold Rally

items.summary: In Xiamen, Fujian Province, rescue teams are working to protect Chinese white dolphins, known as the 'giant pandas of the sea.' These animals rank among the rarest marine species in China's coastal waters. Ecological restoration efforts aim to improve their natural habitat and support recovery for injured and stranded individuals.
items.title: Xiamen Rescue Teams Protect China's Rarest Marine Mammals

items.summary: A CGTN commentator argues that Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has failed to correct a remark linking China's internal affairs to Japan's collective self-defense, which the author calls erroneous. The piece contends this evasion accompanies an accelerating military buildup: fiscal 2026 defense spending exceeded 9 trillion yen (about $56.79 billion), long-range missiles were deployed on March 31, and arms-export restrictions were revised on April 21. Former leaders Yukio Hatoyama and Takeshi Iwaya reportedly called for Japan to withdraw the remarks and repair ties. The author concludes that Japan should honor four political documents and curb military expansion to earn neighbors' trust.
items.title: Japan's Taiwan Remarks and Military Buildup Draw Criticism

items.summary: A CERES-2 Y3 carrier rocket launched at 7:37 am Beijing time on November 7, 2026 from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center. Developed by Galactic Energy, it delivered four satellites into a 535 km sun-synchronous orbit. The upgraded medium-lift vehicle uses three solid stages plus a liquid upper stage, with an approximate liftoff mass of about 100 tonnes and a payload capacity of 1.3 tonnes to a 500 km sun-synchronous orbit.
items.title: Galactic Energy Launches Upgraded CERES-2 Y3 Rocket

items.summary: A gunman shot at people in Kraków's main market square before police detained him near Dietla and Stradomska streets. Witnesses Julek, 67, and Konrad described the sudden dark car and gunfire from its driver's side window; smoke emerged as officers fired back during the arrest. Police report six killed and more than a dozen injured, including two officers who returned fire while others used their weapons to stop him. Reports began around 3 p.m., with police citing military-style clothing and firearms. PM Donald Tusk offered condolences and urged politicians not to exploit the tragedy, promising an investigation into all circumstances of the crime.
items.title: Kraków Square Shooting Leaves Six Dead and Over a Dozen Wounded

items.summary: A gunman drove into Krakow's Main Market Square and opened fire before being shot by police while still alive and arrested. At least six people - four women and two men - are confirmed dead, with at least 15 injured, including two officers who were shot during the arrest; one officer is in very critical condition after three shots. Witnesses described hearing more than 20 shots from multiple firearms. The suspect wore military-style attire and carried a military-grade weapon. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk is heading to Krakow for an address Saturday as investigations continue.
items.title: Krakow Square Attack Leaves Six Dead, Suspect Arrested

items.summary: The US announced a reward of up to $20 million for information about Iran's nuclear programme, with the State Department's Rewards for Justice also offering potential relocation of informants. The offer follows claims that Iran's facilities were destroyed and amid speculation over possible renewed strikes on sites such as Pickaxe Mountain.
items.title: US Offers $20m Reward for Iran Nuclear Information

items.summary: The ninth China International Import Expo opened in Shanghai on November 5, 2026 and runs through November 10. A CGTN commentator argues the event's value lies beyond high-profile innovations such as laparoscopic surgical robots and prototype 6G terminals; instead it showcases upstream industrial chains linking suppliers to end-product developers under one roof. The article presents this 'point-to-sector-to-chain' layout, seen in a semiconductor exhibition area gathering material suppliers, equipment makers, chip designers and downstream firms, as evidence of the expo's evolution from product display toward full-chain collaboration.
items.title: CIIE 2026 reframes expo around full industrial chains, not single exhibits

items.summary: At least six people were killed and 15 injured after a man opened fire from his car on pedestrians near the main market square in Kraków, Poland’s second-largest city. Local police said he fired “at random” around 3pm; authorities described him as an acting-alone Polish citizen wounded during a shootout with officers. Two police officers were hurt, one seriously shot three times. The prime minister and president responded publicly while officials pledged accountability for the perpetrator.
items.title: Six Killed in Random Shooting at Kraków Market Square

items.summary: In early October, Artur Danielyan, leader of Armenia's opposition party Adekvad, was arrested after a Facebook post criticizing Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan. Observers describe this as part of a growing pattern over two years in which Armenian authorities charged multiple opposition figures on social media activity. Civil society groups condemn the case as politically motivated and signal democratic backsliding. A 2025 Freedom House report notes nearly 95% of incitement cases involved threats against Pashinyan. EU analysts say Brussels remains silent, pursuing a pragmatic approach focused on countering Russian influence rather than defending Armenia's rule of law.
items.title: Armenia's Opposition Arrest Draws EU Silence Concern

items.summary: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña, impeached and placed under house arrest Friday after the collapse of Ueno Bank, appeared before prosecutors Saturday morning. He denied wrongdoing but resigned Thursday; lawmakers rejected that resignation and moved forward with impeachment proceedings. Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in to serve until August 2028.
items.title: Ousted Paraguayan President Appears Before Prosecutors

items.summary: Josh Adams scored two tries as Wales won 28-21 over Japan for a bonus point and their third win in five tests. The result eased the burden after an 18-match losing streak following the 2023 World Cup, but coach Steve Tandy noted a lacklustre display with weak set-piece work and poor lineout handling that cost territory. Wales led 21-14 at halftime before Japan held on to 62 per cent possession yet could not convert it into more points ahead of tests against New Zealand and Australia.
items.title: Wales edge Japan in lacklustre Nations Championship clash

items.summary: South Africa's ANC is heading for its worst-ever election performance, with near-final municipal poll tallies showing it gaining just over 30% of the vote. The Electoral Commission reported Saturday that after 98% of votes were counted, the party lost majorities in six of eight metropolitan regions. Voters blame water and electricity shortages on ANC-run municipalities.
items.title: ANC Faces Worst-Ever Result in South African Local Elections

items.summary: A profile traces David Jones, an 188-year-old Sydney department store founded in 1838, from its origins to a present fight for survival. Historian Matthew Bailey frames the car and discount retailers as major disruptors that eroded the service-based model that once dominated Australian retailing. The company's upmarket positioning helped it endure, but historians pinpoint declining detailed customer service since the 1980s as the start of its decline. Chief executive Erica Berchtold says a reset plan is underway with administrators and lenders. Experts say surviving may require vision like founder Sir Charles Lloyd Jones once had.
items.title: David Jones Clings on Amid Retail Decline

items.summary: A single fraud charge led ABC's 7.30 into a black market operating in plain sight, where people sell fraudulent 'cash for demerit points' services that take the blame for driving offences at a cost. The investigation followed one woman charged with fraud who allegedly racked up 1,150 demerit points and more than $600,000 in fines before her arrest in Woodridge, south of Brisbane; Queensland detectives allege she ran the scheme on social media for 'at least four years' after transferring 1,266 traffic infringements into her name. Two other prosecuted cases — Bin Zhang's wider racket between 2012 and 2022 that avoided more than $420,000 in fines across 1,400 false nominations, and Nicholas John Anforth's cocaine-funded operation — show the pattern repeated at commercial scale. The Queensland Revenue Office and Department of Transport and Main Roads declined to answer how they detect fraud or how many drivers escaped suspension; cybersecurity expert David Tuffley said if their systems 'can't see a pattern that obvious' there are no detection controls in place, arguing any future scams should be caught at the fifth transfer, not the 1,200th.
items.title: 7.30 exposes Queensland's demerit points black market

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass in Paysandú, Uruguay, before more than 40,000 faithful at the Parque París Londres. His homily centred on unity and community, opening with "Peace is possible and we are called to build it." This marks his sixth apostolic journey, coming less than a month after lung adenocarcinoma surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Calls for Peace in Uruguay

items.summary: On November 7th, 2026, Euronews aired its evening news bulletin. The program presents a short round-up of the latest stories in world affairs, business, politics, culture, entertainment and travel. Described as reported with independence and a European perspective, it offers viewers a regular overview of current events worldwide.
items.title: Euronews Broadcasts Evening News Round-Up Across Europe and Beyond

items.summary: A gunman drove into Krakow's main market square Saturday afternoon, killing at least six people and wounding more than a dozen, local police said. The perpetrator, a Polish citizen wearing military-style fatigues with a long gun, aimed at random passersby before officers shot and wounded him in the ensuing gunfight; some victims are police officers. Mass shootings remain uncommon in Poland.
items.title: At Least Six Killed in Krakow Shooting

items.summary: At TRT World Forum 2026 in Istanbul, a panel titled Towards a Rocky Recovery examined the economic fallout of regional conflicts. Former OECD Secretary-General Angel Gurria estimated Lebanon would need about $20 billion for reconstruction while Gaza required at least $75 billion. Fabian Zuleeg linked instability to European energy and trade risks; Steve Keen cited public debt rising from 63% to 75% and private-sector debt surging from 55% to 155% over 70 years.
items.title: TRT Forum Panel Weighs Middle East Conflicts and Reconstruction Costs

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass in Paysandu on Saturday, continuing his first Latin American tour as pontiff, which spans 12 days and will also reach Argentina and Peru. The visit marks the first papal trip to Uruguay since John Paul II traveled there in 1988. This is the second day of a three-day stay, with further engagements planned in Montevideo before he departs for Argentina on Sunday.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Opens Latin American Tour with Mass in Uruguay

items.summary: Heavy rain on Saturday flooded tens of thousands of displaced people's tents across war-devastated Gaza, Palestinian authorities said, leaving them without shelter. The Hamas-run government media office reported that about 70,000 tents sheltering tens of thousands of displaced people were flooded on the first day, and noted the collapse of dozens of cracked walls and roofs, which caused injuries. Civil defence spokesman Mahmoud Bassal told AFP his teams received more than 1,500 calls during the night for urgent assistance after their tents flooded, explaining that the agency is operating without any equipment or capabilities.
items.title: Heavy Rains Flood Tents, Displace Thousands in Gaza

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV began a 12-day tour of South America, arriving in Uruguay three weeks after surgery for a tumor on his right lung. He described himself as being 'in fairly good shape' and offered advice to others facing cancer: 'not to be afraid.' The trip includes Masses in Montevideo and Paysandu, visits to Argentina and Peru, where he spent nearly two decades as a missionary.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Opens South American Tour in Fairly Good Shape After Lung Surgery

items.summary: US Amazon Prime customers may receive automatic refunds of up to $200 under a revised settlement with the Federal Trade Commission (FTC), part of a $2. 5 billion deal addressing deceptive enrolment practices and cancellation difficulties. The expanded programme covers members who enrolled between 23 June 2019 and 23 June 2025, used up to 20 Prime benefits in a year, or faced cancellation problems. Payments began on October 1, 2026, running through April 2027 via PayPal, Venmo, or mailed cheques; the final amount depends on fees paid and prior refunds.
items.title: Amazon Prime Refund Eligibility and Claim Details

items.summary: Elon Musk announced on Friday that Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas gigafactory around mid-2027, citing years of persistently weak sales for the model. The company sold 20,237 Cybertrucks in the US last year, down 48% from 38,965 in 2024, far below Musk's predicted annual sales of 250,000 units at launch around the start of production in 2023. Musk said the wind-down would let Tesla make more of the Cybercab robotaxi. Analysts note the shift comes as Chinese rivals gain ground and European markets remain closed to the model over pedestrian-impact rules.
items.title: Tesla Plans Cybertruck Wind-Down Amid Sluggish Sales

items.summary: The Andhra Pradesh Fire Services department issued nearly 5,000 fire no-objection certificates to fireworks vendors through WhatsApp ahead of Diwali. Director-general Venkata Ramana said the facility reduces processing time after field inspections confirmed compliance with safety norms. Every shop had to hold two fire extinguishers and 200 litres of water plus a bucket of sand. Inspections continue across the state.
items.title: Andhra Pradesh Fire Services Issues NOCs via WhatsApp for Diwali

items.summary: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk accused the Ladakh administration on Saturday of witch-hunting him, defaming him, and harassing schools. In a message to President Droupadi Murmu seeking intervention, he alleged that for about six years Ladakh had become a police state with FIRs, arrests over social media activity, and widespread public dissatisfaction with policies favouring corporatisation and liquor bars. Authorities have not responded; on Nov 3 they directed Himalayan Institute of Alternatives to refrain from starting classes at its Leh school pending a high court land dispute case.
items.title: Wangchuk Accuses Ladakh Administration of Witch-Hunt and Smear Campaign

items.summary: After Democrats secured majorities in both chambers of Congress, party leaders are preparing a fast legislative agenda targeting President Donald Trump's policies. Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said the party would 'get out of the gate fast,' prioritizing reversal of Medicaid cuts, restoration of Affordable Care Act tax credits and ending what he called the 'reckless and costly war of choice in Iran.' Chuck Schumer added Democrats could continue pushing even if vetoed, with early bipartisan signs on ACA subsidies. Trump retains his veto power, and most legislation still faces a 60-vote Senate threshold that complicates passage.
items.title: Democrats Prepare Legislative Push Against Trump on Healthcare, Iran and Tariffs

items.summary: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi, writing for her upcoming book Belonging: A Journey of Love and speaking to The Guardian and The Hindu, described the 1975 Emergency imposed by her mother-in-law Indira Gandhi as a mistake. She said she believes Indira eventually came to regret it and felt uneasy during that period. In the book, Sonia wrote that keeping Sanjay Gandhi in check could have prevented much of the damage. She noted the decision divided the family and added that pressure from senior colleagues also played a role, with few around Indira sharing Rajiv Gandhi's views. Sonia said Indira later publicly expressed regret over Emergency excesses after calling fresh elections on January 18, 1977; the Emergency officially ended March 21, 1977. The report is based on her interviews and does not independently verify these claims.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Reflects on Emergency as Mistake in Upcoming Book

items.summary: Samir Arora's Helios Mid Cap Fund added shares of Aurobindo Pharma worth Rs 42.74 crore to its portfolio in October, along with Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses and PVR Inox. It increased its holding in One97 Communication (Paytm) to 5.10 lakh shares from 4.83 lakh, raised Multi Commodity Exchange of India by 51,430 shares, and added Ace Vector as the largest addition among 16 other stocks. The fund's assets under management stood at Rs 2,421 crore as of October 31, 2026, with a CAGR of 20.51% since its March 13, 2025 launch.
items.title: Helios Mid Cap Fund Adds Aurobindo Pharma, Paytm and Others

items.summary: Mohammed Shami, a fast bowler celebrated for his wrist position and seam control, retired on November 6 after ending a 13-year Test career. He finished with 229 wickets in 64 Tests — statistically just outside India’s top five fast bowlers — but the article argues the numbers do not capture his mastery or value to captains who tossed him to break partnerships. Shami was both celebrated for breaking open games and vilified after losses, including when critics questioned his commitment because he is Muslim.
items.title: Mohd Shami Retires After Defining an Era of Indian Pace Bowling

items.summary: The Supreme Court refused to lift the ban on preparing, selling and storing non-vegetarian food near Gujarat's Somnath Temple. A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale declined to interfere with an interim order from the Gujarat High Court that keeps the restrictions active. The dispute began when Gir Somnath District Magistrate issued a notification on 10 August, 2026 covering Prabhas Patan and areas within 500 metres of the temple. Restaurant owners challenged it in the Gujarat High Court; some had reportedly operated there for up to 40 years. The court asked the High Court to decide pending appeals preferably within two months, with a hearing set for 25 November, 2026. Until then, the restrictions remain in force. Senior advocate Huzefa Ahmadi argued against the ban; Solicitor General Tushar Mehta defended it on religious grounds. The court did not deliver a final ruling on legality.
items.title: Supreme Court Keeps Somnath Temple Non-Veg Food Ban in Place

items.summary: A full emergency was declared at Kempegowda International Airport, Terminal 1, in Bengaluru on Saturday after a suspected hijack threat message was discovered inside the lavatory of IndiGo flight 6E-451 en route to Lucknow. The pilots returned the aircraft to origin for security checks; upon landing, airport and aviation authorities took control while an investigation into the note's author continues. IndiGo issued a statement regretting inconvenience as passengers received refreshments until clearances allowed resumption.
items.title: IndiGo flight diverted after hijack note found in Bengaluru airport washroom

items.summary: A special report examines two classroom violence incidents exposing school safety lapses in India. In Sector 20, Panchkula, a six-year-old kindergarten student with special needs was assaulted by an eight-year-old classmate inside an empty room and left unconscious for hours, triggering the principal's suspension, teacher firings, criminal cases under the Juvenile Justice Act and Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, and state-wide audits. Separately, in Raptadu, Andhra Pradesh, a 21-year-old man named Hemant stormed a Class 10 mathematics lesson with a chainsaw, critically injuring one girl student and wounding another who intervened before being apprehended in an Atmakur forest police encounter.
items.title: School Safety Failures Exposed After Panchkula Assault and Andhra Chainsaw Attack

items.summary: The world's biggest Spanish-language musician, Benito Antonio Martínez Ocasio (Bad Bunny), has triggered a linguistic discussion over his use of Caribbean dialect. While the Royal Spanish Academy defines "piquete" as conflict or harm, in Puerto Rico it means confident style—reflected in his song NUEVAYoL. Critics on social media say he does not speak properly and deforms the language, but researchers argue this reflects narrow views of standard Spanish rather than flaws in one artist. Sheila Rodríguez Madera notes Bad Bunny performatizes colonial structures while resisting them; Nathaly Gómez Gómez warns that expanding acceptance may reinforce Caribbean hegemony over other Latin American dialects.
items.title: Bad Bunny's Puerto Rican Spanish sparks linguistic debate

items.summary: In her memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love, Sonia Gandhi recounts the turmoil she faced as the Congress party went through a difficult period in the late 1990s. She had always disliked politics and struggled over whether to enter public life after the assassination of her husband Rajiv Gandhi before the Bhagavad Gita helped her decide. Her children Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi argued fiercely with her because they feared losing her too. Sonia says she became a primary member of the Congress in 1997 after party president Sitaram Kesri invited her to its plenary session, then reflected on Krishna's message before deciding to step into politics.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Recounts Turning to Bhagavad Gita Before Entering Politics

items.summary: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath, addressing seers at the 10th edition of Deepotsav in Ayodhya on Saturday, demanded an apology to 'Ram Bhakts' before Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav visits the Ram temple there. Speaking without naming Yadav directly, Adityanath said those who fired on karsevaks during the October 30 and November 2, 1990 events under Mulayam Singh Yadav's government must first apologise to seers and residents before seeking blessings. Akhilesh Yadav is set to visit with his family on December 12, his first since January 2024 consecration. SP leader Pawan Pandey countered that faith should not be politicised. Seers welcomed the remarks with 'Jai Shri Ram.'
items.title: Yogi Adityanath Demands Apology Before Akhilesh Yadav's Ayodhya Visit

items.summary: The Conversation has published an article listing the five novels on the Booker Prize 2026 shortlist, describing each as written by its contributor. Luke Kennard's Black Bag is called a campus comedy inspired by a 1967 Oregon State University experiment; M John Harrison's The End of Everything imagines alien-induced collapse on the Kent coast and quotes his own writing about piling up real facts to reveal something unreal; Elizabeth Strout's The Things We Never Say follows Artie Dam, a Massachusetts Bay high school teacher nominated for the prize three times before; Marlon James's The Disappearers is set in Jamaica from 1988 to 2005 and concerns gay men who vanish without notice; and Rebecca Perry's debut May We Feed The King tells of a person obsessed with a medieval king remembered only for his faults. All five entries are presented as selections meant to inspire readers across different tastes.
items.title: The Conversation names a diverse Booker Prize 2026 shortlist

items.summary: During Diwali, several temples in Madhya Pradesh were decorated with large displays of cash, gold and silver. In Mandsaur, the Agarwal community organised ornaments worth over Rs 4.5 crore plus 100 kg of silver and 2 kg of gold at Mata Lakshmi Temple; more than 200 families contributed. A similar display in Nyaypati Topwale Balaji Temple featured notes over Rs 80 lakh, while Bhadwa Mata Temple in Neemuch was decorated with currency worth Rs 5.51 lakh. The displays remain open until Nov 11.
items.title: Diwali Treasures Adorn MP Shrines With Crores in Cash, Gold and Silver

items.summary: Two fires broke out Saturday night in Mumbai high-rises. A blaze on the 17th floor of Runwal Elegante in Lokhandwala, Andheri West, was confined to electrical wiring and household articles inside Flat No. 1701; it took over an hour to control and was extinguished at 10:37 pm with no injuries reported, a fire official said. Separately, a fire broke out in the gallery of Flat No. 1901 on the 19th floor of Moroccan Apartment in Royal Palms, Goregaon East; it was confined to an area about 10 x 15 feet and extinguished at 9:52 pm with no injuries reported. The exact causes remain under investigation.
items.title: Fire Breaks Out On 17th Floor Of Runwal Elegante In Andheri, Another Blaze Reported At Goregaon High-Rise | Video

items.summary: Police recovered a decomposed body from Yercaud forest, the third so far linked to alleged killings by cab driver Indusekar alias Sekar over about two weeks. He allegedly murdered seven members of his wife’s family across Karnataka and Tamil Nadu; police suspect he may have given sedatives and are probing possible abetment by his minor daughter. Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge said questioning continues, with more information expected in another two to three days.
items.title: Karnataka Police Recover Third Body in Bengaluru Murder Case

items.summary: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee challenged the BJP on Saturday after Abhishek Banerjee, her Diamond Harbour constituency colleague and three-time MP, alleged that BJP-backed miscreants accompanied by police personnel attacked his residence in Kalighat around 2 am or 3 am. Condemning what she called atrocities and intimidation amid restrictions under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), Mamata 'dared' the BJP to use its bulldozers against her, telling police: 'If you have the courage, come and run your bulldozers over my body.' She said the incident reflected lawlessness in the state, accused the party of hypocrisy for holding Save Democracy rallies while blocking pujas at her Patuapara home, warned officers to stay neutral or she would fight them, threatened to approach the Supreme Court, and called a minute's silence. PTI reported the statements.
items.title: Mamata Banerjee Defies BJP With Bulldozer Threat After MP's Home Attack

items.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath asked Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav to apologise to kar sevaks before entering the Ram Temple in Ayodhya, referring to the 1990 police firing during Mulayam Singh Yadav's tenure. Speaking at the 10th Deepotsav event on November 7, Adityanath said those who once insulted devotees must repent first. Akhilesh had separately announced a December 12 visit with wife Dimple Yadav.
items.title: Yogi Adityanath Demands Apology from Akhilesh Yadav Before Ayodhya Visit

items.summary: Political Editor Anand Mishra of Frontline opens a newsletter by noting speculation that friction between Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and former CM Siddaramaiah stems from an alleged sting operation, with loyalist K.N. Rajanna calling for its investigation while Shivakumar allies attack him in return. The row prompts Mishra to explore the widespread Indian political practice of touching feet as a gesture of respect or submission across Congress, BJP, socialist and regional parties, citing examples from Sonia Gandhi's visit to Lalu Prasad's residence through Chirag Paswan's repeated gestures toward Nitish Kumar, ending with reflections on whether such acts reflect cultural tradition or sycophancy. He signs off noting more on the Shivakumar–Siddaramaiah issue appears in a later Frontline edition. Mishra is Political Editor at Frontline.
items.title: Indian Political Editor Reflects on Feet-Touching Culture Across Parties and States

items.summary: Foreign institutional investors bought more than the Rs 45,162 crore withdrawn by overseas investors in October, reversing recent outflows. FIIs were net buyers across all five trading sessions, extending their buying streak to a second consecutive week after a 10-week selling spell. Domestic institutions turned net sellers for the first time in 12 weeks, offloading Rs 24,197 crore as they booked profits. The inflows coincided with one of the strongest weekly rallies in benchmark indices: the Nifty rose 8.57% to close at 25,030 and the Sensex climbed 8.82% to settle at 81,028 on Friday, November 6.
items.title: FIIs pump Rs 45,960 crore into Indian stocks in a week; is the tide finally turning for Dalal Street?

items.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government announced a hike in the Dearness Allowance (DA) for state employees, raising the rate to 63 percent effective July 1, 2026. The revised DA will be paid with November salaries and covers government employees plus aided educational institutions, technical institutions, and urban local bodies across the state. Arrears from July to October 2026 will be credited into employees' PF accounts depending on their arrangements: GPF after tax deductions for most; NPS members receive 10 percent in Tier-I pension accounts while the remaining 90 per cent goes to Public Provident Fund or National Savings Certificates.
items.title: Uttar Pradesh Raises Dearness Allowance to 63 Percent Ahead of Diwali
